data.description: Bug #2 from the AS-7 first-fire shakeout (see AS-7 comment 2026-08-30). Deadlock in the lock protocol: apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs fire() acquires apps/chat/data/advance.lock (source:'watcher', watcher pid) BEFORE spawning claude -p '/advance'. The spawned tick runs advance.md step 0, sees a fresh lock it cannot attribute to itself, and no-ops. advance.md already says 'ticks fired by the message watcher skip this step' — but the spawned tick cannot detect that it IS watcher-fired: the headless invocation is byte-identical to a manual one. Every watcher-fired tick therefore self-cancels. Evidence: apps/chat/data/logs/tick-2026-08-30T18-08-30.241Z.log (tick exited 0, 'Tick ended as a no-op — lock is held', lock pid 17730 == live watcher pid). DESIGN (decided by cto-owen, rationale in plan): watcher passes ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT=watcher:<pid> in the tick child env; advance.md step 0 changes to: a lock whose source is 'watcher' AND whose pid matches ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT is YOUR lock — proceed, and do NOT release it (the watcher releases its own lock in settle() on tick exit); locks from any other source/pid are foreign — no-op. Requires widening the AS-14 env pin {PATH,HOME,USER,LOGNAME} by exactly this one documented variable in tickChildEnv() plus its pin test. Alternatives rejected: (a) watcher releases the lock pre-spawn and lets the tick take its own — opens a real race window between release and the child's step 0 where a manual tick or loop steals the slot, and breaks the watcher's settle()/timeout ownership semantics; (b) advance.md adopts ANY fresh source:watcher lock without a marker — misfires when a manual tick races a watcher fire: the manual tick would adopt the watcher's lock and proceed, defeating single-flight. The env marker is deterministic parent identification: no race, no ambiguity, one documented env var. advance.md is employee-editable; the step-0 wording change is in scope for the implementer.
data.title: Watcher-fired ticks self-cancel on the watcher's own advance.lock — pass ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT marker so the tick recognizes its parent's lock

data.body: Planning done (cto-owen). Plan at .lattice/plans/task_01M19XVZRGFF7QCHR8QRT01BQN.md, branch feat/AS-15-watcher-lock-marker (38580a4). Design: ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT=watcher:<pid> in tickChildEnv (env pin widens {PATH,HOME,USER,LOGNAME} by exactly this one documented var + pin test update in test/watcher.test.js ~L288), and advance.md step 0 reworded: source:watcher lock whose pid matches the marker is YOUR lock — proceed, never release it (watcher's settle() releases); any other source/pid is foreign — no-op. Rejected pre-spawn release (race window, breaks settle()/timeout ownership) and markerless adoption of fresh watcher locks (manual tick racing a watcher fire would adopt the watcher's lock). Note for implementer: advance.md is employee-editable; the step-0 wording is in scope. No lock-acquisition logic changes — the lock stays etiquette, not load-bearing.

Implementation done (developer-marcus), commit 6dc193a. tickChildEnv(env, watcherPid) now returns exactly {PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT} with ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT='watcher:<pid>'; fire() passes process.pid; spawn-site comment documents the variable's reason per AS-14. Pin test widened to 5 vars + marker format/pid assertions, including no leak-through of an ancestor's marker from the source env. advance.md step 0: source 'watcher' + pid == ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT is your lock, proceed and never release (watcher settle() releases); any other source/pid foreign -> no-op; manual/loop path unchanged. Suite in-container: 92/92 pass. No lock-acquisition changes in the watcher; no watcher restart performed.

QA review (qa-priya, cold, branch feat/AS-15-watcher-lock-marker, diff master...branch): PASS — all 3 acceptance criteria met, no inline fixes needed. [AC1] tickChildEnv returns exactly {PATH,HOME,USER,LOGNAME,ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT} with marker 'watcher:<pid>' — verified by code read, by direct execution (source env polluted with ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT=watcher:99999 + SHELL yields exactly the 5-key set with watcher:4242; default arg = process.pid), and by the widened pin test. Suite in-container: 92/92 pass (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose run --rm test), matching the implementer's claim. Leak-test falsifiability confirmed: the deepEqual asserts a literal watcher:4242, so a leaked ancestor marker cannot pass. [AC2] advance.md step 0 states the full rule (source 'watcher' + pid == ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT is YOUR lock, proceed, never release; watcher settle() releases; any other source/pid foreign -> no-op); manual/loop wording untouched. Never-release consistency: step 5 releases only 'if this tick created it' — the watcher created this lock, so no strand/double-release path exists in the text. TIMEOUT path consistent: settle() runs on the exit event including SIGTERM/SIGKILL-after-timeout, releaseLock() is pid-guarded, and lockStaleMin(45) > tickTimeoutMin(30) keeps the freshness math sound. [AC3] No other env vars added; no lock-acquisition changes (diff touches only tickChildEnv signature, the spawn call, and comments). Attack — marker spoofing with a stale ADVANCE_TICK_PARENT in a foreign shell: wrongful adoption requires lock.source=='watcher' AND lock.pid == marker pid AND that pid alive with a fresh lock; a dead marker-watcher's lock hits the stale-steal path instead. Residual window is exact-pid reuse by a new live watcher coinciding with a leaked env — filed as backlog hardening (per-fire nonce in lock+marker), non-blocking: lock is etiquette per file header, violates no stated criterion. Noted for the record: CLAUDE.md one-sentence edit ('Use the most reasonable model...') rode along in plan commit 38580a4 (cto-owen) — top-level-md metawork ride-along per convention, presumed board/orchestrator, not touched. Verdict: PASS — ready for done + merge by the orchestrator.
